author: Stannis
text_post: Personality is way too vague and overencompassing a term to be used as a counterpart to looks. Looks are the primary determinant of attraction, but attraction is only one factor (and not even necessarily an elementary one) in relationships. I don’t think such instances as reanimated observed can be rationalised away by money or status.  Or that actual primal attraction exists in these dynamics. Physical closeness and companionship, though inorganic and forced if not built on primal attraction, seem to emulate the neurochemical responses of the transference happening during immediately apparent mating compatibility, even if over a over a progression of time and at a much lower intensity. I always perceived it as an evolutionary contingency measure. If no optimal mate is available, people instinctively work their way down the ladder with regards to what is in their immediate proximity and barely adequate in a lot of cases. Then rationalisation mechanisms kick in and make these people delude themselves into a specious state of bliss when in reality they’re settling for their best accessible option. To safeguard a temporal stability in the relationship. The simplest explanation for such aesthetic discrepancies as observed in the OP is accessibility. People settling, pure and simple, for the sole purpose of not being alone. And they’re not even actively cognisant of it. The human capacity for self-delusion is immense. They’re actually thinking that’s what they want when really it’s was the most uncomplicated thing they could get. Those women are happy dating below their league, they feel affection for their partner. But as soon as a better and viable long-term option comes along they’ll pull a 180 and flee the scene. And you can’t overstate the importance of social approval. On an external level the fact of not having single status and the capability to externally project happiness is important. On another having a sensible partner with the potentiality for long term stability also contributes to the former. This is where practical considerations factor in. The preppy yuppie girl might be more drawn to the small time drug dealer or brooding artist due to looks on a primal level, but  they’re not viable options and will subject her the scrutiny of her peers. Which is why you rarely see couple constellations like that. Women want physical companionship, and they want to be able to showcase that they are capable of maintaining a stable relationship. And they're willing to date down for that. Which is how things like OP’s mall observations can be explained.

author: Stannis
text_post: EDIT: Didn't realise I responded to this thread already. Probably rehashed the exact same thing. Disregard. I honestly don't think that this is a trend exclusive to millennials. I quite frankly encounter more aesthetically mismatched couples in my day to day than the other way around and I’ve given this quite a bit of thought. I can only rationalise with an evolutionary perspective as it being a contingency measure to ensure the perpetuation of the species in case of a viable high quality mate being absent or inaccessible. Most couples don’t seem to result from instant primal attraction but from recurring exposure. Women likely also feel such thing as an acute intransitive sexual need that is not necessarily tied to a specific person. In the above scenario, i.e. absence of high quality mate, a woman will settle and sleep with a guy she deems ‘guy enough’. On repeated occasion (due to convenience and propinquity) it will autogenerate a less intense emulation of the neurochemical process in place in the case of primal attraction. Another factor is her deluding herself that she has deep feelings for her partner, because that not being the case would threaten her perception of her perfect life. She might grow attached to him, she might have deep affection for him, she might enjoy the sex irrespective of him but she will never love him or feel raw sexual attraction for him. It’s effectively a self-sustaining positive feedback loop where the male is instrumentalised. Being physically close to someone, having someone invested in you feels good to women and makes them react positively and mirror that behaviour. Naturally it would feel infinitely better if they could have the above with a prime mate, but ‘good enough’ seems to be the leitmotif in most relationships. Add to that the fact that a prime mate is generally in higher demand, has more options and is less likely to commit, so women intuitively opt for a safer guy. A lot of people feel pressure to follow a preset life script. In that vein being in a relationship is a goal in and of itself and they’re more than willing to compromise even if they’re not consciously aware that they’re doing so. They’re probably not even cognisant of the fact that their feelings for their partner are basically  tepid or completely synthetic until they’re confronted with someone they feel primal attraction for.  It’s essentially nature’s fallback plan ensuring that people procreate even if the resulting child will be of suboptimal genetic stock. At least that’s how I think of it.
